score.doctor_final_text:
The X-ray confirms no fracture, which tells me this is a pure tendon avulsion rather than a bony injury. Given the classic mechanism — your finger caught in a jersey with forced extension while gripping — combined with your complete inability to flex the fingertip and tenderness on the palm side of the DIP joint, I'm confident in the diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey finger (avulsion of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon of the right ring finger) — this requires urgent referral to a hand surgeon for surgical repair.

dialogue.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I understand you're having progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger — how long has this been going on?
It started about 2 days ago when I was playing football. My finger got caught in another player's jersey and he pulled away really hard.
Got it — that mechanism is important. Can you bend the tip of your ring finger on your own, at the last joint near the fingertip?
No, I can't bend it at all at that last joint. When I try to make a fist, that fingertip just stays straight while the rest of my fingers curl in normally.
That's very telling — is there tenderness or a lump anywhere along the palm side of your finger or into your palm, as if something has bunched up there?
Yes, there's definitely tenderness right at that last joint on the palm side of my finger. I don't really feel a distinct lump though, just swelling and it's pretty sore when I press on it.
That mechanism and inability to flex the fingertip strongly suggest a tendon injury — let me get imaging to check for a bone fragment. REQUEST TEST: Finger_X-Ray
RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand shows no bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.
